overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair's emails distributing draft documents were for discussion at a future noticed meeting, though commentary was cautioned against. The 2018 Boelter notice says this 2015 ruling may be superseded.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair deliberated with members by emailing them a draft response to a complaint and a letter from the complainant before a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that because the documents were distributed for the purpose of discussion at a future meeting, rather than for the purpose of expressing an opinion to the other Committee members, this did not violate the law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair's emails to members, which included his own commentary on the letters, were improper because they expressed opinions outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: While the circumstances here do not rise to the level of an Open Meeting Law violation, we caution against any commentary when distributing documents for discussion at a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
